title: Microsoft Azure
subtitle: Azure hosts the Windows side of my Teams integration: a media bridge with managed identity, vault-held secrets and authenticated access.

buffer rate held across the soak

lede: Microsoft Teams hands raw call audio only to a Windows application built on Microsoft's real-time media SDK. The speech models and conversation engine behind Helix run on Linux GPUs, and I was not going to send call audio to someone else's AI service to get around that. I put the smallest possible piece in Azure and kept the brain on my own hardware. That piece is a .NET 8 media bridge on an Azure Windows Server virtual machine. The region turned down two smaller VM sizes for lack of capacity, so it runs on a larger general-purpose size.
quote: I use the cloud for exactly the part of a system that has to live there.
evidence: Cloud architecture with a minimal footprint: only the Windows media bridge on Azure, with managed identity, Key Vault and no open inbound ports.
Soak testing for real-time media: 91,643 buffers in a 30-minute soak at 50.001 per second with zero stalls.
Ephemeral compute for AI jobs: Container Apps Jobs that exist only for their run, with cleanup checks leaving 0 executions active.
author: Corey James
